course_summary:
ISEN 625 | Simulation Methods and Applications | Spring 2026
Instructor: David Eckman | eckman@tamu.edu
Meets: TR 09:35AM-10:25AM | ZACH 345; M 1:50PM-4:20PM | ETB 2026
Grading: Attendance [4%], Participation [6%], Lab Assignments [10%], Quizzes [10%], Midterm Exam [35%], Final Exam [35%]
Topics: OptQuest, KN method, Kernel density estimation, Parameter estimation (MLE), Chi-square test, K-S test, Q-Q plots, Uniform random variates, Inversion (random-variate generation), Acceptance rejection (random-variate generation), Non-stationary arrival process, Reliability logic, Custom run setup, User defined statistics, Simulation by hand, Conceptual modeling, Input modeling, Empirical data, Resampling, Data tables, Counting (simulation), Branching (simulation), Plots (simulation), Interpreting results (simulation), Sequences (simulation), Transporters (simulation), Linking with data tables, Work schedule (simulation), Function (simulation), Use of lists (simulation), Processes (simulation), Common random numbers, Terminating simulation, System comparison, Simulation-based optimization, Random number generation, Variate generation, Random-variate generation, Arrival processes, Input analysis, Output analysis, Statistical analysis of model output, Simulation data preparation, Discrete event modeling, Discrete event (process-oriented) simulation modeling, Fundamental methodologies of simulation modeling, Verification, Validation, Confidence intervals, Bootstrapping, Error vs risk, Visualization, Histograms, Probability and statistics review, Critical thinking, Quantitative reasoning, Simulation
Tools: Python, Simio, Jupyter notebooks, Canvas
Prerequisites: STAT 212 or STAT 601
